newsitem.title: ITALY: Boehler sees lower 1997 pretax profit.
newsitem.headline: Boehler sees lower 1997 pretax profit.

text.p: Austrian highgrade steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm AG said on Friday it expected 1997 group pretax profit to come in below the level posted in 1996 while operating profit would likely hold steady.
"The year 1997 will be the toughest year in comparison to the last three years," chief executive Claus Raidl told journalists during a visit to Italy.
"The target is for our operating profit to match that of 1996," he said, while pretax profit would be lower due to the absence of extraordinary income.
For 1996, Boehler expects to have posted a pretax profit of 1.2-1.3 billion schillings after 1.35 billion in 1995, and an operating profit of around one billion.
Raidl said the dividend would be around the same as the year before, but declined to give further details. In 1995, Boehler paid out a 25 schilling dividend.
Under its restructuring programme, Boehler plans to reduce its workforce in 1997 to under 9,000 from 9,200.
